title: Nest the card and filter with :has()
prompt:
Three jobs, all in CSS:

1. Rewrite the three `.session-card` rules (base, `h2`, `:hover`) as **one nested rule** on `.session-card`.
2. When the `#hide-full` checkbox is checked, hide (`display: none`) every `.session-card` that contains a `.badge-full`.
3. When a card's `.save` checkbox is checked, give that card a `#6d28d9` border color.

Don't add JavaScript or change the HTML.
hints: Inside the `.session-card` rule, `h2 { … }` and `&:hover { … }` replace the separate rules.
For the filter, start from the ancestor that contains both the checkbox and the cards: `.schedule:has(#hide-full:checked)`.
`.schedule:has(#hide-full:checked) .session-card:has(.badge-full) { display: none; }` and, nested in the card, `&:has(.save:checked) { border-color: #6d28d9; }`.
explanation: Nesting keeps every state of the card in one block: `h2` becomes a descendant rule and `&:hover` attaches the pseudo-class to the card itself. The filter works because `.schedule` contains both the checkbox and the cards: `:has(#hide-full:checked)` turns the checkbox state into a condition on that shared ancestor, and `.session-card:has(.badge-full)` picks out sold-out cards. The save highlight is the same idea one level down: the card matches `:has(.save:checked)` as soon as its own checkbox is ticked, and the browser re-evaluates both rules on every change, with no JavaScript.

checks.uses-nesting: The card styles use native nesting
checks.all-visible: All cards are visible before filtering
checks.hides-sold-out: Checking the filter hides only the sold-out card
checks.shows-again: Unchecking the filter shows it again
checks.saved-highlight: A saved card gets a violet border
